title: Proverbs 18
paragraphs: ¹ An unfriendly person pursues selfish ends and quarrels with sound judgment. ² A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, only in airing their own opinions. ³ When wickedness comes, so does contempt, and with shame comes disgrace. ⁴ The words of a person's mouth are deep waters; a fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook. ⁵ It is not good to show partiality to the wicked and so deprive the innocent of justice.

⁶ The lips of a fool invite conflict, and their mouth invites a beating. ⁷ The mouth of a fool is their ruin, and their lips are a trap for their life. ⁸ The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down into the stomach. ⁹ One who is slack in their work is a sibling to one who destroys. ¹⁰ The name of the LORD is a fortified tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.

¹¹ The wealth of the rich is their fortified city; they imagine it a wall too high to scale. ¹² Before a downfall the heart is haughty, but humility comes before honor. ¹³ To answer before listening — that is folly and shame. ¹⁴ The human spirit can endure sickness, but who can survive a crushed spirit? ¹⁵ The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.

¹⁶ A gift opens the way and ushers the giver into the presence of the great. ¹⁷ The first to speak in court seems right, until the other comes and cross-examines. ¹⁸ Casting lots settles disputes and keeps strong opponents apart. ¹⁹ An offended friend is harder to win back than a fortified city; disputes are like the barred gates of a citadel. ²⁰ The mouth of a person satisfies their stomach; the produce of their lips fills them.

²¹ The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love to talk will eat what it produces. ²² Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing and receives favor from the LORD. ²³ The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly. ²⁴ A person with many friends may be ruined by them, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
